title: Qt: Make sequence graph Comment column width adjustable
description:
Add a QCPAxisTickerText subclass that, when the associated
QCPAxis has a fixed margin, elides the label to fit within that
margin.

Use that for the comment axis. Allow clicking on the comment axis to
select it, and then have mouse dragging it while selected resize the
comment axis rectangle margin, which will also cause the labels to
automatically update.

Fix #4972

I cannot make this work on macOS. Should I be able to resize the Comment column in a regular Flow Graph?

It requires clicking once on the axis to select it:
![image](/uploads/4cbf1871f1a5a48c5a7e11169f860207/image.png)

and clicking a second time near it once it is selected to drag it (because of the order in which it's processed.)

That might not be user-friendly enough. I can take away the need to have the axis already selected, and just allow dragging to start if the mouse is clicked near enough, although perhaps drawing a line for the axis at all times would be useful.

Try commenting out the `if (yAxis2->selectedParts().testFlag(QCPAxis::spAxis)) {` test in `void SequenceDialog::diagramClicked(QMouseEvent *event)` and always setting `axis_pressed_ = true;` if the event position is close to the right side of the axis rectangle and see if that works for you.

I would never be able to figure this by myself, so my guess is that it should be improved. I would expect to be able to select between the headers to change size, like we have in all other tables/lists.
Is !16244 any easier? It doesn't require a two-step process, just clicking in the vicinity of the axis line. Double-clicking the comment column will also auto-resize it.

Yes this is slightly better, this I'm able to find without reading documentation. Still feels a bit alien compared to our other widgets. The blue "ladder" line looks strange, and it's not possible to move the dotted lines for an endpoint. And the pointer does not change to a "resize" icon. But all-in-all this is better than nothing.

> The blue "ladder" line looks strange

Eliminated the ticks when the axis is selected by setting the tick length to zero.

> And the pointer does not change to a "resize" icon. 

The pointer should change to and from `Qt::SplitHCursor` now.

> it's not possible to move the dotted lines for an endpoint.

Right, that one is only keyboard (+ and -) and it would be nicer to have a mouse control for it.
I think the splitter cursor really adds to discoverability, good suggestion.

+/** @file
+ *
+ * QCustomPlot QCPAxisTickerText subclass that elides labels to the
+ * width of the parent QCPAxis's QCPAxisRect's margin for the appropriate
+ * side, for use when the margin is fixed.
+ *
+ * Copyright 2024 John Thacker <johnthacker@gmail.com>
+ *
+ * Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+ * By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
+ * Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs
+ *
+ * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+ */
+
+#ifndef QCP_AXIS_TICKER_ELIDED_H
+#define QCP_AXIS_TICKER_ELIDED_H
+
+#include <ui/qt/widgets/qcustomplot.h>
+
+class QCPAxisTickerElided : public QCPAxisTickerText
+{
+public:
+    explicit QCPAxisTickerElided(QCPAxis *parent);
+
+    // QCP has marginSideToAxisType but not the inverse
+    static QCP::MarginSide axisTypeToMarginSide(const QCPAxis::AxisType);
+
+    QString elidedText(const QString& text);
+
+protected:
+    virtual QString getTickLabel(double tick, const QLocale &locale, QChar formatChar, int precision) override;
+
+private:
+    QCPAxis *mParent;
+};
+
+#endif
